1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.

The present civil misc. appeal has been filed by the appellant
Magan Lal vs Smt.Uma @ Ombala And Ors ... on 8 September, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42775860/

1 - Magan Lal against the judgment and award dated 06.09.2003 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhinmal, District Jalore (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal"),
whereby, the claim petition filed by Smt. Uma and Omprakash was allowed (Uploaded on 09/09/2025 at 03:20:06 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:39637] (2 of 4) [CMA-60/2004] and a compensation of Rs.82,000/- (Rupees Eighty Two Thousand Only) was awarded.
3. Briefly noted the facts in the present appeal are that on 16.09.1997, Naresh son of Omprakash was standing in front of his house when a Tanker being driven by Khima Ram dashed into Naresh, due to which, he suffered multiple injuries in the accident and while being taken to the hospital, he succumbed to those injuries.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhinmal, District Jalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In these circumstances, a claim petition was filed by the claimants before the learned Tribunal and the learned Tribunal, after evaluating the evidence and deliberating on the four issues recorded a finding that since the driver of the Tanker was not holding a valid and effective licence at the time of accident, therefore, the Insurance Company was not liable for payment of compensation and since the appellant was the owner of the Tanker, both the driver and owner were held responsible for payment of compensation awarded in the present case.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently argued that the appellant is not responsible for payment of compensation in the present case.
However, he is unable to satisfy this Court that the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal are contrary to the evidence on record and have been erroneously recorded.

5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has supported the judgment passed by the learned Tribunal and has submitted that the finding of fact recorded on issue No.3 clearly goes to show that Khima Ram was driving the Tanker at the time of accident without a valid and effective licence.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to satisfy the award of compensation passed by the learned court below.
He (Uploaded on 09/09/2025 at 03:20:06 PM)
[2025:RJ-JD:39637] (3 of 4) [CMA-60/2004] further submits that even Khima Ram has been charged under Section 3/181 of Motor Vehicle Act for driving the Tanker without licence.

He,
therefore, prays that the judgment passed by learned Tribunal does not suffer from any infirmity.
6. I have considered the submissions made at the Bar and have gone through the relevant record of the case.

7. The factum of the accident has been proved beyond doubt before the learned Tribunal and on the claim petition filed by the claimants, learned Tribunal has framed four issues, which are reproduced as under:-

sentences.text: On the issue No.1, a finding has been recorded by the learned Tribunal that at the time of accident, the Tanker was being driven by Khima Ram rashly and negligently, thereby causing the accident in which Naresh sustained injuries and ultimately succumbed to those injuries.

The finding recorded on issue No.3 also clearly shows that at the time of accident, the vehicle was being driven by Khima Ram, who was the khalasi of the Tanker and that he was not holding a valid and effective licence for driving the vehicle.

Therefore, the finding on issue No.3 was recorded in favour of the Insurance Company, and the driver and owner of the Tanker were held responsible for payment of (Uploaded on 09/09/2025 at 03:20:06 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:39637] (4 of 4) [CMA-60/2004]
compensation in the present case.

As far as issue No.2 is concerned, an amount of Rs.82,000/-
(Rupees Eighty Two Thousand Only) has been awarded by the learned Tribunal after taking into consideration the computation of loss caused to the claimants on account of the death of Naresh,
who was a child of one and a half years.
9. Upon a close reading of the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal on all the three issues, this Court finds that there is no inconsistency and the same does not suffer from any infirmity.
The findings have been recorded after due application of mind and after taking into consideration the evidence placed on record.
10. In the considered opinion of this Court, no interference is warranted in the judgment dated 06.09.2003 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhinmal, Dist. Jalore.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhinmal, Dist. Jalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 11. The appeal, therefore, has no merit, the same is therefore, dismissed.
